data.title: Qualcomm Stock Slides After Handset Sales Drop Raises Margin Pressure Questions
data.description:
• Qualcomm reported Q4 2026 and full year results with handset chip revenue down 26% and issued Q1 FY27 revenue guidance of US$10.4b to US$11.2b, highlighting weaker smartphone demand and ongoing cost pressure despite growth in automotive, IoT and data center activities.
  • The business is leaning harder on newer engines such as automotive, custom AI data center programs and long term 5G infrastructure agreements with SpaceX. However, these segments are still in ramp mode and have not fully offset the handset driven squeeze on chip segment margins.
  • The focus now turns to what this Qualcomm earnings reset and handset driven margin pressure could mean for the existing investment narrative.

QUALCOMM Investment Narrative Recap

To stay comfortable owning QUALCOMM, you need to believe the handset slump is a manageable reset while non handset lines such as automotive, IoT and AI data centers scale into something more balanced. The latest quarter and Q1 FY27 revenue guide of US$10.4b to US$11.2b keep that story intact but show how dependent near term sentiment still is on smartphones and chip input costs.

The key near term catalyst remains execution on the data center and automotive ramps, because those areas are starting to matter more to the mix and to how investors frame QUALCOMM’s future earnings power. The biggest current risk is that handset demand and rising manufacturing costs continue to pressure QCT margins faster than new programs, including AWS and other hyperscale wins, can contribute.

The SpaceX Starlink Mobile 5G infrastructure deal looks most relevant here. It extends QUALCOMM beyond devices into carrier grade 5G and AI ready networking, with deployment planned from 2027 and revenue contribution expected toward late fiscal 2027 and more fully in 2028. That timing lines up with management’s push to have non handset QCT revenue, including data center and automotive, carry more of the load.

This agreement also increases execution risk. QUALCOMM now has to deliver at scale on Starlink Mobile at the same time it ramps custom AI data center silicon for AWS and other hyperscalers, all while handset revenue and Apple modem exposure are under pressure. For you, the question is whether the combination of these long dated contracts offsets the margin squeeze and smartphone cyclicality that have driven the latest earnings reset.

QUALCOMM's current analyst narrative assumes revenue grows at 10.8% a year and points to earnings today of US$9.3b, rising to a consensus forecast of US$11.5b by 2029, an increase of about US$2.2b, with revenues projected to reach US$60.0b in the same year.

data.title: Gold.com, Inc. Just Missed Earnings - But Analysts Have Updated Their Models
data.description:
The analysts might have been a bit too bullish on Gold.com, Inc. (NYSE:GOLD), given that the company fell short of expectations when it released its first-quarter results last week. Gold.com delivered a grave earnings miss, with both revenues (US$3.3b) and statutory earnings per share (US$0.05) falling badly short of analyst expectations. Earnings are an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance, look at what the analysts are forecasting for next year, and see if there's been a change in sentiment towards the company. So we gathered the latest post-earnings forecasts to see what estimates suggest is in store for next year.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Following the recent earnings report, the consensus from four analysts covering Gold.com is for revenues of US$21.5b in 2027. This implies a not inconsiderable 14% decline in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory per-share earnings are expected to be US$2.90, roughly flat on the last 12 months. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of US$21.5b and earnings per share (EPS) of US$2.74 in 2027. So the consensus seems to have become somewhat more optimistic on Gold.com's earnings potential following these results.

See our latest analysis for Gold.com

The consensus price target was unchanged at US$64.40, implying that the improved earnings outlook is not expected to have a long term impact on value creation for shareholders. It could also be instructive to look at the range of analyst estimates, to evaluate how different the outlier opinions are from the mean. The most optimistic Gold.com analyst has a price target of US$90.00 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at US$52.00. As you can see, analysts are not all in agreement on the stock's future, but the range of estimates is still reasonably narrow, which could suggest that the outcome is not totally unpredictable.

These estimates are interesting, but it can be useful to paint some more broad strokes when seeing how forecasts compare, both to the Gold.com's past performance and to peers in the same industry. These estimates imply that revenue is expected to slow, with a forecast annualised decline of 19% by the end of 2027. This indicates a significant reduction from annual growth of 24% over the last five years. By contrast, our data suggests that other companies (with analyst coverage) in the same industry are forecast to see their revenue grow 3.2% annually for the foreseeable future. It's pretty clear that Gold.com's revenues are expected to perform substantially worse than the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The biggest takeaway for us is the consensus earnings per share upgrade, which suggests a clear improvement in sentiment around Gold.com's earnings potential next year. On the plus side, there were no major changes to revenue estimates; although forecasts imply they will perform worse than the wider industry. The consensus price target held steady at US$64.40, with the latest estimates not enough to have an impact on their price targets.

Following on from that line of thought, we think that the long-term prospects of the business are much more relevant than next year's earnings. We have forecasts for Gold.com going out to 2029, and you can see them free on our platform here.

data.title: The Andersons, Inc. Just Beat EPS By 23%: Here's What Analysts Think Will Happen Next
data.description:
It's been a sad week for The Andersons, Inc. (NASDAQ:ANDE), who've watched their investment drop 14% to US$55.12 in the week since the company reported its third-quarter result. Revenues of US$2.8b fell slightly short of expectations, but earnings were a definite bright spot, with statutory per-share profits of US$1.36 an impressive 23% ahead of estimates. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. So we gathered the latest post-earnings forecasts to see what estimates suggest is in store for next year.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Following the latest results, Andersons' three analysts are now forecasting revenues of US$11.8b in 2027. This would be a satisfactory 6.5% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to accumulate 2.8% to US$6.28. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of US$11.9b and earnings per share (EPS) of US$6.40 in 2027. The consensus analysts don't seem to have seen anything in these results that would have changed their view on the business, given there's been no major change to their estimates.

See our latest analysis for Andersons

It will come as no surprise then, to learn that the consensus price target is largely unchanged at US$86.67. The consensus price target is just an average of individual analyst targets, so - it could be handy to see how wide the range of underlying estimates is. There are some variant perceptions on Andersons, with the most bullish analyst valuing it at US$90.00 and the most bearish at US$80.00 per share. With such a narrow range of valuations, the analysts apparently share similar views on what they think the business is worth.

Taking a look at the bigger picture now, one of the ways we can understand these forecasts is to see how they compare to both past performance and industry growth estimates. For example, we noticed that Andersons' rate of growth is expected to accelerate meaningfully, with revenues forecast to exhibit 5.2% growth to the end of 2027 on an annualised basis. That is well above its historical decline of 7.1% a year over the past five years. Compare this against analyst estimates for the broader industry, which suggest that (in aggregate) industry revenues are expected to grow 5.1% annually. So it looks like Andersons is expected to grow at about the same rate as the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing to take away is that there's been no major change in sentiment, with the analysts reconfirming that the business is performing in line with their previous earnings per share estimates. Happily, there were no real changes to revenue forecasts, with the business still expected to grow in line with the overall industry. There was no real change to the consensus price target, suggesting that the intrinsic value of the business has not undergone any major changes with the latest estimates.

data.title: Can Elicio Therapeutics (NASDAQ:ELTX) Afford To Invest In Growth?
data.description:
Even when a business is losing money, it's possible for shareholders to make money if they buy a good business at the right price. For example, although software-as-a-service business Salesforce.com lost money for years while it grew recurring revenue, if you held shares since 2005, you'd have done very well indeed. Having said that, unprofitable companies are risky because they could potentially burn through all their cash and become distressed.

Given this risk, we thought we'd take a look at whether Elicio Therapeutics (NASDAQ:ELTX) shareholders should be worried about its cash burn. In this report, we will consider the company's annual negative free cash flow, henceforth referring to it as the 'cash burn'. The first step is to compare its cash burn with its cash reserves, to give us its 'cash runway'.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

How Long Is Elicio Therapeutics' Cash Runway?

You can calculate a company's cash runway by dividing the amount of cash it has by the rate at which it is spending that cash. When Elicio Therapeutics last reported its September 2026 balance sheet in November 2026, it had zero debt and cash worth US$31m. Looking at the last year, the company burnt through US$38m. Therefore, from September 2026 it had roughly 10 months of cash runway. That's quite a short cash runway, indicating the company must either reduce its annual cash burn or replenish its cash. You can see how its cash balance has changed over time in the image below.

How Is Elicio Therapeutics' Cash Burn Changing Over Time?

Because Elicio Therapeutics isn't currently generating revenue, we consider it an early-stage business. So while we can't look to sales to understand growth, we can look at how the cash burn is changing to understand how expenditure is trending over time. It's possible that the 3.2% reduction in cash burn over the last year is evidence of management tightening their belts as cash reserves deplete. Clearly, however, the crucial factor is whether the company will grow its business going forward. So you might want to take a peek at how much the company is expected to grow in the next few years.

How Easily Can Elicio Therapeutics Raise Cash?

Even though it has reduced its cash burn recently, shareholders should still consider how easy it would be for Elicio Therapeutics to raise more cash in the future. Issuing new shares, or taking on debt, are the most common ways for a listed company to raise more money for its business. One of the main advantages held by publicly listed companies is that they can sell shares to investors to raise cash and fund growth. By looking at a company's cash burn relative to its market capitalisation, we gain insight on how much shareholders would be diluted if the company needed to raise enough cash to cover another year's cash burn.

In the last year, Elicio Therapeutics burned through US$38m, which is just about equal to its US$37m market cap. Given just how high that expenditure is, relative to the company's market value, we think there's an elevated risk of funding distress, and we would be very nervous about holding the stock.

So, Should We Worry About Elicio Therapeutics' Cash Burn?

Even though its cash burn relative to its market cap makes us a little nervous, we are compelled to mention that we thought Elicio Therapeutics' cash burn reduction was relatively promising. The ex-dividend date is an important date to be aware of as any purchase of the stock made on or after this date might mean a late settlement that doesn't show on the record date. Meaning, you will need to purchase Diamondback Energy's shares before the 12th of November to receive the dividend, which will be paid on the 19th of November.

The company's next dividend payment will be US$1.18 per share, on the back of last year when the company paid a total of US$4.72 to shareholders. Calculating the last year's worth of payments shows that Diamondback Energy has a trailing yield of 2.6% on the current share price of US$178.96. Dividends are an important source of income to many shareholders, but the health of the business is crucial to maintaining those dividends. Diamondback Energy has delivered 28% dividend growth per year on average over the past nine years. Things were not great overall, with a surprise (statutory) loss of US$0.03 per share on revenues of US$89m, even though the analysts had been expecting a profit. The analysts typically update their forecasts at each earnings report, and we can judge from their estimates whether their view of the company has changed or if there are any new concerns to be aware of. We thought readers would find it interesting to see the analysts latest (statutory) post-earnings forecasts for next year.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

Taking into account the latest results, the current consensus from UroGen Pharma's seven analysts is for revenues of US$539.7m in 2027. This would reflect a major 116% increase on its revenue over the past 12 months. Earnings are expected to improve, with UroGen Pharma forecast to report a statutory profit of US$2.76 per share. In the lead-up to this report, the analysts had been modelling revenues of US$522.8m and earnings per share (EPS) of US$2.76 in 2027. So it looks like there's been no major change in sentiment following the latest results, although the analysts have made a small lift in to revenue forecasts.

View our latest analysis for UroGen Pharma

The consensus price target increased 5.9% to US$61.71, with an improved revenue forecast carrying the promise of a more valuable business, in time. There's another way to think about price targets though, and that's to look at the range of price targets put forward by analysts, because a wide range of estimates could suggest a diverse view on possible outcomes for the business. The most optimistic UroGen Pharma analyst has a price target of US$75.00 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at US$56.00. Analysts definitely have varying views on the business, but the spread of estimates is not wide enough in our view to suggest that extreme outcomes could await UroGen Pharma shareholders.

Looking at the bigger picture now, one of the ways we can make sense of these forecasts is to see how they measure up against both past performance and industry growth estimates. The analysts are definitely expecting UroGen Pharma's growth to accelerate, with the forecast 85% annualised growth to the end of 2027 ranking favourably alongside historical growth of 28% per annum over the past five years. Compare this with other companies in the same industry, which are forecast to grow their revenue 21% annually. It seems obvious that, while the growth outlook is brighter than the recent past, the analysts also expect UroGen Pharma to grow faster than the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The most obvious conclusion is that there's been no major change in the business' prospects in recent times, with the analysts holding their earnings forecasts steady, in line with previous estimates. Happily, they also upgraded their revenue estimates, and are forecasting them to grow faster than the wider industry. We note an upgrade to the price target, suggesting that the analysts believes the intrinsic value of the business is likely to improve over time.

Keeping that in mind, we still think that the longer term trajectory of the business is much more important for investors to consider. We have forecasts for UroGen Pharma going out to 2028, and you can see them free on our platform here.

That said, it's still necessary to consider the ever-present spectre of investment risk. We've identified 3 warning signs with UroGen Pharma (at least 1 which doesn't sit too well with us) , and understanding these should be part of your investment process.

data.title: Selling US$1.3m Of Ironwood Pharmaceuticals Stock Rewarded Insiders
data.description:
Despite a 25% gain in Ironwood Pharmaceuticals, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:IRWD) stock price this week, shareholders shouldn't let up. Even though stock prices were relatively low, insiders elected to sell US$1.3m worth of stock in the last year, which could indicate some expected downturn.

While we would never suggest that investors should base their decisions solely on what the directors of a company have been doing, we do think it is perfectly logical to keep tabs on what insiders are doing.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Ironwood Pharmaceuticals Insider Transactions Over The Last Year

The CEO & Director, Thomas McCourt, made the biggest insider sale in the last 12 months. That single transaction was for US$740k worth of shares at a price of US$3.81 each. That means that even when the share price was below the current price of US$4.39, an insider wanted to cash in some shares. As a general rule we consider it to be discouraging when insiders are selling below the current price, because it suggests they were happy with a lower valuation. Please do note, however, that sellers may have a variety of reasons for selling, so we don't know for sure what they think of the stock price. It is worth noting that this sale was only 24% of Thomas McCourt's holding.

Ironwood Pharmaceuticals insiders didn't buy any shares over the last year. You can see a visual depiction of insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last 12 months, below. By clicking on the graph below, you can see the precise details of each insider transaction!

See our latest analysis for Ironwood Pharmaceuticals

If you are like me, then you will not want to miss this free list of small cap stocks that are not only being bought by insiders but also have attractive valuations.

Insider Ownership Of Ironwood Pharmaceuticals

Another way to test the alignment between the leaders of a company and other shareholders is to look at how many shares they own. I reckon it's a good sign if insiders own a significant number of shares in the company. Insiders own 3.2% of Ironwood Pharmaceuticals shares, worth about US$22m. While this is a strong but not outstanding level of insider ownership, it's enough to indicate some alignment between management and smaller shareholders.

So What Do The Ironwood Pharmaceuticals Insider Transactions Indicate?

There haven't been any insider transactions in the last three months -- that doesn't mean much. We don't take much encouragement from the transactions by Ironwood Pharmaceuticals insiders. The modest level of insider ownership is, at least, some comfort. So while it's helpful to know what insiders are doing in terms of buying or selling, it's also helpful to know the risks that a particular company is facing. data.title: Why Is Micron Technology (MU) At The Center Of A Global Chip Selloff?
data.description:
• Micron Technology (NasdaqGS:MU) is at the center of a sharp global selloff in semiconductor stocks tied to recent company setbacks.
  • The group has paused construction work at a plant site in Taiwan, raising questions about its future capacity plans in the region.
  • Investors are reacting to fresh concerns that post election US rules on AI infrastructure could tighten and affect Micron's business model.
  • Trading in chip makers across US tech indices and Korea's Kospi has turned volatile as markets reassess exposure linked to Micron's Taiwan plant pause and possible tighter US AI rules. Yet there is more to this story than today's shock. We have also flagged 4 other big wins for Micron Technology.

For a broader view on how AI hardware spending and regulation are shaping opportunities, it is worth examining 52 AI infrastructure stocks.

Micron Technology is a US based memory and storage producer that supplies chips used in data centers, AI servers and consumer electronics across Taiwan, Mainland China, other Asia Pacific markets, Japan, Europe and the US. Any disruption to its footprint can ripple across global supply chains.

Does the team leading Micron Technology have what it takes? See our full breakdown of the management team's track record and compensation.

Why has news around Micron Technology sparked such a broad semiconductor selloff?

Micron’s halted Taiwan plant construction, combined with fresh concerns about tighter US rules on AI data centers after the elections, has become a stress test for memory exposed stocks. Markets are quickly repricing how much AI driven demand can offset labor disputes, higher capital needs and possible regulatory friction for data center buildouts.

Does this change the Micron Technology Narrative investors have been leaning on?

The current shock leans straight into the Narrative’s key risk that heavy capex and tight DRAM or NAND conditions could be upset by execution problems in new fabs or labor constraints. At the same time, the news does not touch the core catalyst described there, long term customer agreements tied to AI memory that aim to turn tight supply into durable cash generation.

See how these catalysts shape Micron Technology's path to a $1,561 fair value.

How do leadership changes and board retirement plans feed into Micron’s direction?

Linnie M. Haynesworth plans to retire from the board after the January 2027 meeting, which will reduce Micron’s directors to eight and remove a chair with deep security and aerospace experience from its Security Committee. Investors will be watching how remaining committees absorb that portfolio and whether a successor reinforces areas like cybersecurity and AI infrastructure oversight.

What is the single development to watch next for Micron Technology after this selloff?

The clearest signal will be Micron’s next detailed update on its Taiwan buildout and US AI focused capacity plans, including whether the Taoyuan construction pause alters timelines, capex totals or its multi year supply commitments through 2030. A firm reaffirmation or reset of those concrete targets would either support or challenge the current Narrative built on tight supply and locked in demand.

The Micron Technology question markets rarely ask out loud
